data.title: TGV SRAAC (NSE:TGVSL) Posted Healthy Earnings But There Are Some Other Factors To Be Aware Of
data.description:
TGV SRAAC Limited's (NSE:TGVSL) stock was strong after they recently reported robust earnings. However, we think that shareholders may be missing some concerning details in the numbers.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

Examining Cashflow Against TGV SRAAC's Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. The ratio shows us how much a company's profit exceeds its FCF.

That means a negative accrual ratio is a good thing, because it shows that the company is bringing in more free cash flow than its profit would suggest. While it's not a problem to have a positive accrual ratio, indicating a certain level of non-cash profits, a high accrual ratio is arguably a bad thing, because it indicates paper profits are not matched by cash flow. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

For the year to September 2026, TGV SRAAC had an accrual ratio of 0.23. Therefore, we know that it's free cashflow was significantly lower than its statutory profit, which is hardly a good thing. Even though it reported a profit of ₹1.57b, a look at free cash flow indicates it actually burnt through ₹2.1b in the last year. It's worth noting that TGV SRAAC generated positive FCF of ₹1.4b a year ago, so at least they've done it in the past. The good news for shareholders is that TGV SRAAC's accrual ratio was much better last year, so this year's poor reading might simply be a case of a short term mismatch between profit and FCF. Shareholders should look for improved cashflow relative to profit in the current year, if that is indeed the case.

Our Take On TGV SRAAC's Profit Performance

TGV SRAAC didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Therefore, it seems possible to us that TGV SRAAC's true underlying earnings power is actually less than its statutory profit. The good news is that, its earnings per share increased by 29% in the last year. The shares cost £6.41 at the start of the period, and anyone looking at Vistry Group then had to decide which of two stories felt more convincing.

On the upbeat side, one narrative saw fair value at £7.73 and focused on UK affordable housing demand and offsite manufacturing. That view assumed revenue could grow 11.9% a year with profit margins rising from 2.0% to 6.1% by about 2028.

The opposing case put fair value at £4.50 and treated slower UK housing demand as the anchor. Here, revenue was expected to decline 0.4% a year, even though margins were still assumed to climb from 2.0% to 6.6% by 2028, with heavy dependence on government funding as a central risk.

The clearest new fact for Vistry Group was the reported H1 2026 loss of £607 million on revenue of £1,418.2 million. Net margin moved from 1.9% in H1 2025 to a loss at 42.8%, so the profitability step-up in both the bullish and cautious narratives was not yet delivered. This evidence supported the cautious case more than the optimistic one.

The hinge here was earnings quality, not sentiment. For any other builder you look at, test upbeat margin stories against reported net income and net margin, especially after big restructuring promises.

data.title: Cisco (CSCO) Stock Can Q1 Results Sustain The AI Rebound?
data.description:
Cisco Systems came into this earnings print with a stock that had slipped over the past month and quarter, then jumped 2.2% to US$97.18 on the first full trading day after results. The reputation is that of a steady, utility-like networking giant, but the fresh Q1 2027 numbers tell a sharper story.

Revenue for the quarter landed at US$18.5b and basic earnings per share reached about US$1.15. Profit from ongoing operations over the last twelve months totaled roughly US$15.0b. The key question now is whether this profit increase justifies the recent price rebound.

Like the consistency of Cisco Systems earnings but want a cleaner balance between income and future resilience? Check out our list of solid balance sheet and fundamentals stocks (24 results) for a set of stocks built around robust fundamentals and stronger financial cushions.

Q1 2027 Earnings Summary

  • Revenue (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$18.52b vs. US$14.88b (up about 24.3%)
  • Net Income from Ongoing Operations (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$4.55b vs. US$2.86b (up about 59.2%)
  • Basic EPS (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): US$1.15 vs. US$0.72 (up about 59.5%)
  • Trailing Twelve Month Net Margin (Q1 2027 vs. Q1 2026): 22.3% vs. 17.9% (margin level improved year over year)

Earnings are one thing, especially when Cisco Systems is putting up Q1 numbers like these, but investors who care about what they are paying often focus on the cash coming in and out of the business.

On Cisco Systems' cash flows alone, and using the platform's discounted cash flow work, the stock could be a clear 26% undervalued.

Cisco’s Bullish AI And Refresh Thesis On Trial

The bullish analyst Narrative on Simply Wall St argues that Cisco Systems can use AI demand and a large internal refresh wave to reset its earning power.

"The main thing that has to go right is Cisco Systems successfully converting its identified upgrade and refresh pool and hyperscaler AI orders into profitable, recurring business while managing hardware mix and margin pressures."

Q1 shows Cisco Systems hitting key milestones on that claim. Hyperscaler and cloud orders climbed strongly, with AI infrastructure now guided to about US$9b in FY27 and backed by a sizeable backlog. Recurring metrics also moved in the right direction, with ARR at US$32.7b and RPO at US$46.2b, which supports the idea that more of this demand is being locked in as ongoing business rather than one-off projects.

Not everyone reads the same price the same way. → See the higher figure this Narrative lands on, and how it gets there.

Cisco Bear Case: Hardware Mix Risks Under Review

The bearish analyst narrative on Simply Wall St focuses on Cisco Systems taking on heavier hardware exposure that could undermine earnings quality.

"Ongoing mix shift toward high volume hardware for AI data centers, while software and total ARR currently grow at low single digit rates, could limit the contribution of higher margin recurring revenue and make overall profitability more sensitive to hardware cycles and pricing."

Q1 shows some of that concern in the numbers. Product revenue moved ahead much faster than services and software ARR only grew 4%. Product gross margin of 63.7% was under pressure even as non GAAP operating margin reached 37.8%, so the profitability impact of this mix shift remains unresolved.
